stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Slide $A$ (mass number) and $Z$ (atomic number) to build a nucleus. Orange dots are protons, teal are neutrons. The chart on the right places the isotope on the $(Z, N)$ map — the green band is the stability zone. Advance after visiting at least $5$ different elements.
stages.concept: A nucleus is described by two counts: $Z$ (protons, fixes the element) and $A$ (total nucleons). $N = A - Z$ is the neutron count. Two nuclei with the same $Z$ but different $A$ are isotopes of the same element. The nucleus symbol $^{A}_{Z}X$ bundles all three: mass number, atomic number, element symbol.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Build each named target isotope by setting $A$ and $Z$. The element name tells you $Z$; the number after the dash is $A$.
stages.concept: Isotope name $\to$ composition: the element name determines $Z$ (Carbon means $Z = 6$, Uranium means $Z = 92$). The dash-number is the mass number $A$. Then $N = A - Z$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: You're given only $Z$ and $N$. Pick the correct isotope name from the four choices. The element symbol on the nucleus is hidden this time.
stages.concept: Reverse mapping: given $(Z, N)$, first compute $A = Z + N$, then look up the element from $Z$. The full label is then $\text{Element-}A$. Distractors will differ by $Z$ (wrong element) or by $A$ (wrong isotope of the right element).

labels.tip1: slide A and Z; watch protons + neutrons rearrange
labels.tip2: element name → Z; number after dash → A
labels.tip3: A = Z + N; then look up the element from Z

1.1: Z is the number of protons — it fixes the element. Try sliding just Z.
1.2: A is the total nucleon count. If you fix Z and change A, you're making isotopes of the same element.
1.3: You need to visit 5 different Z values. Slide Z through H (1), He (2), C (6), O (8), etc.

2.1: For Carbon-14: Carbon means Z = 6. The 14 is the mass number A. Set A = 14, Z = 6.
2.2: For Oxygen-16: Oxygen is Z = 8. A = 16, so N = 8.
2.3: For Uranium-235: Uranium is Z = 92 (biggest natural element). A = 235 — a big neutron count.

3.1: Compute A first: A = Z + N. Then figure out which element has that Z.
3.2: Watch for distractors that share Z (same element, wrong A) or share A (right A, wrong element).
3.3: Z = 6 always means Carbon. Z = 2 means Helium. Z = 92 means Uranium.
